categories.name: SSD Storage
categories.tagline: Expand console storage for 100+ GB story installs without constant uninstalls.
categories.description: Picks drawn from 2025–2026 console storage roundups (Tom’s Hardware, TechSpot, and PS5 heatsink fit guides). We only list PCIe 4.0 NVMe drives that clear Sony’s ~5,500 MB/s bar and ship with a console-safe heatsink—plus clear notes when Xbox Series needs a different path (licensed Expansion Card or USB archive).
categories.consoleAngle: PS5 / PS5 Pro: install a heatsinked PCIe 4.0 M.2 in the expansion bay. Xbox Series X|S: use a Seagate/WD licensed Expansion Card for full-speed installs; USB externals are for media and cold storage only.

products.name: WD_BLACK SN850X 2TB with Heatsink
products.summary: Still the default PS5 upgrade in 2026 roundups: factory heatsink that fits the expansion bay, sequential reads up to 7,300 MB/s, and 2 TB that actually covers a modern story library plus patches. Tom’s Hardware keeps the SN850X as its best overall PS5 SSD for performance-per-dollar.
products.bestFor: Most PS5 owners who want one internal install and forget about it
pros: Heatsink SKU (WDS200T2XHE) fits the PS5 bay without a third-party cooler
Consistently clears Sony’s official speed requirement in reviews
2 TB + 5-year warranty is the sweet spot for large day-one titles
cons: Heatsink model costs more than the bare stick
Xbox Series still needs a licensed Expansion Card for full-speed internal play

products.name: Crucial T500 2TB with Heatsink
products.summary: When the SN850X heatsink is on sale-tax territory, the T500 with factory cooler is the value Gen4 pick reviewers keep naming: up to 7,400 MB/s read, PS5-compatible heatsink, and 2 TB of Micron TLC without stepping down to a USB external.
products.bestFor: PS5 players who want internal Gen4 speed at a lower street price
pros: Integrated heatsink meets PS5 height/thermal guidance
Often undercuts brand-premium heatsink SKUs at the same capacity
5-year limited warranty and strong sustained write reviews
cons: Street price swings; confirm the heatsink SKU (CT2000T500SSD5)
Less “name brand” shelf appeal than WD or Samsung

products.name: Samsung 990 PRO 2TB with Heatsink
products.summary: Premium pick when you want the fastest mature Gen4 platform with a slim PS5-rated heatsink. Review sites now treat the post-firmware 990 PRO as a top alternate to the SN850X—especially if Magician tooling or brand support matters to you.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want peak Gen4 reads and a thin official heatsink fit
pros: Up to 7,450 MB/s sequential read on the heatsink SKU
Ultra-slim cooler designed around PS5 bay clearance
Samsung Magician support if you also use the drive in a PC later
cons: Usually costs more per TB than SN850X / T500
Buy the heatsink model (MZ-V9P2T0CW)—bare sticks need a separate cooler

categories.name: Headsets
categories.tagline: Hear story dialogue and positional cues without drowning the mix.
categories.description: Console-first picks from 2026 headset guides that emphasize platform reality: Xbox needs Xbox-certified wireless, PS5 is flexible with USB dongles, and a 3.5 mm jack still wins for zero-setup nights. We favor long-session comfort, usable boom mics, and dual wireless where it actually helps.
categories.consoleAngle: Prefer the Xbox (“X”) wireless SKU when you play both consoles—those dongles usually cover PS5/PC too. Wired 3.5 mm works on DualSense and Xbox controllers. Sony Pulse gear is excellent on PS5/Portal but not a dual-console default.

products.name: SteelSeries Arctis Nova 7X Wireless Gen 2
products.summary: Best cross-console wireless pick in current guides: USB-C 2.4 GHz dongle that covers Xbox, PS5, and PC, simultaneous Bluetooth for calls, and up to ~50 hours of battery. ClearCast Gen 2 boom and AirWeave pads keep party chat and long campaigns usable.
products.bestFor: Households that hop between Xbox and PlayStation
pros: One Xbox-certified dongle that also works on PS5 / PC
2.4 GHz + Bluetooth mix so phone audio does not kill game audio
Retractable noise-rejecting boom and long battery life
cons: App EQ depth is still better on PC than on pure console
Pricier than a simple wired set if you never leave one platform

specs.platformNotes: Xbox / PS5 / PC / Switch via USB-C dongle

products.name: HyperX Cloud III Wired
products.summary: The durable wired classic updated for modern consoles: angled 53 mm drivers, memory-foam pads, aluminum frame, and a clear detachable boom. Ships with 3.5 mm plus USB-C/A paths so DualSense, Xbox, and Switch all stay simple—no battery anxiety on launch night.
products.bestFor: Budget console players who want reliable chat and comfort
pros: Works on PS5 / Xbox / Switch without proprietary dongles
No batteries or firmware drama
Swappable cushions and a tough metal frame
cons: Wired only—cable management is on you
Spatial audio depends on the console/platform software

specs.platformNotes: Controller jack or USB on PS5 / Xbox / Switch

products.name: PlayStation Pulse Elite
products.summary: Premium PS5 immersion: planar magnetic drivers, lossless PlayStation Link wireless, retractable AI noise-reject mic, and up to 30 hours of battery. TechRadar and other 2026 guides still call it the best official PlayStation headset—especially if you also use a Portal.
products.bestFor: PS5 / Portal players chasing dialogue detail and Tempest 3D
pros: Planar drivers deliver cleaner dialogue and staging
PlayStation Link works with PS5, Portal, PC, and Mac
Bluetooth dual-connect for calls without dropping game audio
cons: Not an Xbox wireless headset
Bulkier fit than lighter SteelSeries Nova models

specs.platformNotes: Best on PS5 / Portal; PC via Link adapter

categories.name: TVs & Monitors
categories.tagline: Display picks tuned for console HDMI 2.1, VRR, and HDR story nights.
categories.description: Living-room and desk picks grounded in 2025–2026 gaming TV tests (What Hi-Fi?, Tom’s Guide, RTINGS-class feature checks). Priority order: four full-bandwidth HDMI 2.1 ports, VRR + ALLM, honest 4K120 console paths, and brightness that matches your room—not PC-only 240 Hz marketing.
categories.consoleAngle: PS5 and Xbox Series X need HDMI 2.1 with VRR/ALLM for the full feature set. A 144 Hz OLED helps PC later, but consoles top out at 4K120. Bright living rooms may prefer Mini-LED over OLED.

products.name: LG C5 55" OLED evo
products.summary: 2025 C-series is the console living-room default in current awards: four HDMI 2.1 ports, VRR/ALLM/G-Sync/FreeSync, Dolby Vision gaming, and brighter OLED evo panels than the C4. What Hi-Fi? and Tom’s Guide both land on the C5 as the best all-round gaming TV for PS5 and Xbox.
products.bestFor: Couch console play in a light-controlled room
pros: Four full-bandwidth HDMI 2.1 ports for console + soundbar
Excellent contrast for cinematic single-player
Mature Game Optimizer with VRR, ALLM, and HGiG
cons: Still not as bright as top Mini-LED sets in sunny rooms
Static HUDs for years raise OLED burn-in risk

products.name: LG UltraGear 27GS75Q-B 27"
products.summary: Desk or dorm console pick: sharp 1440p IPS, 180 Hz panel, FreeSync / G-Sync Compatible VRR, and HDMI inputs that keep PS5/Xbox looking crisp up close. You give up living-room 4K OLED drama, but HUD text and aim clarity stay excellent under $200.
products.bestFor: Bedroom / office console setups where 27" beats a huge TV
pros: Sharp 1440p text and HUDs
High refresh for smoother camera pans
Console-friendly Adaptive-Sync / FreeSync path
cons: Not a 4K living-room TV replacement
HDR is modest compared with OLED / Mini-LED TVs

products.name: Samsung QN90D 65" Neo QLED
products.summary: Bright-room premium: Mini-LED punch that keeps HDR readable with the curtains open, four HDMI 2.1 ports, 4K120 gaming, and a 65" canvas for couch co-op. Choose this over OLED when daylight and peak highlights matter more than perfect black floors.
products.bestFor: Sunny living rooms that still want 4K120 console gaming
pros: Excellent peak brightness for daytime play
65" shared-view size for couch sessions
Full 4K120 + VRR / ALLM console feature set
cons: Contrast can’t match OLED in a dark room
No Dolby Vision (HDR10+ / HDR10 instead)

categories.name: Capture Cards
categories.tagline: Record and stream console footage without turning your living room into a PC LAN.
categories.description: Creator picks based on 2026 capture-card buyer guides after Elgato retired the HD60 X. We rank for honest HDMI pass-through (so your TV keeps 4K/HDR/VRR), USB convenience for laptop streamers, and capture headroom that matches real Twitch/YouTube encode targets—not brochure fantasy.
categories.consoleAngle: PS5 and Xbox Series output HDMI; match pass-through to your display (4K60 vs 4K120). Most live streams still encode at 1080p60—buy 4K capture only if you archive or edit in 4K.

products.name: Elgato Game Capture 4K S
products.summary: The current mid-tier default now that HD60 X is discontinued: USB-C capture up to 4K60 with 4K60 HDR/VRR pass-through, plus high-frame 1440p/1080p modes. Works cleanly with PS5 and Xbox Series into OBS without needing a desktop PCIe slot.
products.bestFor: Most console streamers and highlight editors buying new
pros: 4K60 capture replaces the old HD60 X ceiling
4K60 HDR / VRR pass-through keeps the TV happy
Mature Elgato + OBS ecosystem on USB-C
cons: HDMI 2.0 class—not for 4K120 pass-through setups
Needs a solid USB bandwidth path and encode CPU/GPU

products.name: Elgato Game Capture Neo
products.summary: Entry creator box that still does the important part right: 4K60 HDR pass-through to your TV while capturing 1080p60 for Discord clips, TikTok, and first OBS streams. Smaller learning curve and lower price than 4K S / 4K X.
products.bestFor: First-time console clip creators on a laptop
pros: Affordable Elgato reliability with real 4K60 HDR pass-through
USB plug-and-play for PC, Mac, and iPad workflows
Compact enough to travel to a friend’s couch
cons: Capture tops out at 1080p60
Skip it if you already need 4K archives or 4K120 pass-through

products.name: Elgato Game Capture 4K X
products.summary: Premium external card for high-refresh living rooms: HDMI 2.1 pass-through up to 4K144 with VRR, and capture headroom up to 4K144 over USB 3.2 Gen 2. Ideal when your Series X / PS5 Pro display runs 4K120 and you refuse to drop the TV to 4K60 just to stream.
products.bestFor: 4K120 console setups that still want USB (no PCIe install)
pros: HDMI 2.1 keeps 4K120 gameplay intact on the TV
High-frame capture options beyond typical 1080p60 streams
Still portable versus an internal PCIe card
cons: Needs a true USB 3.2 Gen 2 port for full modes
Overkill if you only ever stream 1080p60
